visa.title: Australian Medical Treatment Visa (Subclass 602)
visa.intro: The <visaName>Subclass 602 Medical Treatment visa</visaName> allows you to travel to Australia for medical treatment not available or accessible in your home country. MTA patients apply for this visa category.
visa.whoBody: Patients seeking specialist medical or dental treatment in Australia, and their companions or carers.
visa.processingBody: Typically 4–8 weeks. Apply well in advance of your treatment date to avoid delays.
visa.lengthBody: Granted for the period necessary for treatment. Extensions can be applied for if treatment is prolonged.
visa.companionsBody: Immediate family members or a carer may be included on the same application.
visa.officialPage: Official Australian Department of Home Affairs page

documents.title: Preparing Your Documents
documents.intro: The following documents are typically required for a Subclass 602 visa application. Your assigned visa lawyer will confirm the exact requirements for your case.
documents.item0: Valid passport (minimum 6 months validity beyond intended stay)
documents.item1: Hospital invitation letter (provided by MTA after treatment confirmation)
documents.item2: Proof of sufficient funds (bank statements, sponsor letter)
documents.item3: Medical records and specialist reports relevant to your treatment
documents.item5: Two recent passport-sized photographs (as per Australian requirements)
documents.item6: Health insurance or evidence of ability to cover medical costs
documents.item7: Statutory declaration of financial support (if sponsored)

flights.title: Flights
flights.intro: MTA partners with hospitals across Australia’s major cities. Fly into the airport closest to your treatment location:
flights.tip0: Book a <flexFare>flexible fare</flexFare> where possible — treatment dates may shift.
flights.tip1: Consider <travelInsurance>travel insurance</travelInsurance> that covers medical cancellations.
flights.tip2: MTA does not book flights — this section is guidance only.

accommodation.title: Accommodation
accommodation.intro: Staying close to your hospital reduces stress during your treatment period.
accommodation.tip0: <servicedApartments>Serviced apartments</servicedApartments> are popular for longer stays — they offer kitchen facilities and more space than hotel rooms.
accommodation.tip1: <hotelRooms>Hotel rooms</hotelRooms> suit shorter treatment periods or companions travelling separately.
accommodation.tip2: Look for properties within 2–5 km of your hospital for easy access to appointments.
accommodation.tip3: MTA does not book accommodation. Your visa lawyer or MTA coordinator can suggest options specific to your hospital location.

airport.title: Airport & Transport
airport.intro: All major Australian airports are well-connected to city centres and hospital districts.
airport.tip0: <taxiRideshare>Taxis and rideshare</taxiRideshare> (Uber, DiDi) are available at all airports — no pre-booking required.
airport.tip1: <airportTrains>Airport trains</airportTrains> operate in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Perth.
airport.tip2: <shuttleBuses>Shuttle buses</shuttleBuses> are often available for hotels near hospitals — check with your accommodation provider.
airport.tip3: If you have <mobilityNeeds>mobility needs</mobilityNeeds>, notify your airline and accommodation in advance. Australian airports are fully accessible.

preArrival.title: Pre-Arrival Checklist
preArrival.intro: Complete the following before departing for Australia.
preArrival.item0: Visa approved and visa grant letter downloaded
preArrival.item1: Hospital appointment date and contact details confirmed
preArrival.item2: Flights booked with flexible fare for date changes
preArrival.item4: Travel insurance purchased (including medical evacuation cover)
preArrival.item5: Emergency contact informed of your travel plans
preArrival.item6: Sufficient funds accessible (local ATM and card access)
preArrival.item8: MTA contact details saved on your phone
